findings.title: Building interiors keep the exterior window glow instead of DFU's WindowStyle.Disabled (black)
findings.claim: DFU lays out interior models with SetClimate(..., WindowStyle.Disabled) (DaggerfallInterior.cs:473/:517/:1270); Disabled sets EmissionColor black (MaterialReader.cs:934-936). Port: interiorContext.js:120 uploads window masks via uploadRecord (dataPipeline.js:89-91); drawMesh binds them (renderer.js:1578) times the global _windowEmission (renderer.js:1114-1115), which is only ever day/night/fog: main.js:67 boots it 'day'; world.js:3295 / exterior.js:1607 write it only in exterior frames (world.js:3070 modal return exits first); worldModes' interior block (:2779-2796) never calls setWindowEmission; WINDOW_STYLES (windowEmission.js:8-13) has no disabled entry.
findings.consequence: Inside every shop/tavern/house, window glass glows pale blue by day and amber at night where DFU/classic show unlit glass; contradicts the port's own bible (Rendering-Arc R2 note: 'emission stays dark (Disabled)').

findings.title: Dispatcher's Day window style overrides the ?interior scene's documented dark emission
findings.claim: main.js:67 runs renderer.setWindowEmission(windowEmissionRGB(params.get('window') || 'day')) BEFORE routing (the ?interior route is line 68), overwriting the renderer's black boot value (renderer.js:468). interior.js:28-30 documents the DFU law it relies on - 'SetClimate with WindowStyle.Disabled - emission stays dark here by default' - and neither interior.js nor interiorContext.js ever calls setWindowEmission, so 'by default' meant the renderer's boot state, which the dispatcher line defeats. The standalone-scene slice of the previous finding: the port disagrees with its own comment one import away.
findings.consequence: The standalone ?interior dev scene draws climate-swapped window records with a day-blue glow instead of the dark glass the scene header and DFU (MaterialReader.cs:934-936) both specify.

findings.title: ?novideo also skips the audio bootstrap, silencing the classic title/menu music
findings.claim: On the classic-skin path the only pre-menu ensureAudio calls are main.js:164 (inside the '!params.has(novideo)' block at :145) and launcherScene.js:41 (reached only via main.js:127: ?launcher or ShowOptionsAtStart, which the launcher exists to turn off). With ?novideo and ShowOptionsAtStart=False, no AudioContext exists before runMenu: music.playSong needs audio.ctx (music.js:105), created only by audio.ensure (audio.js:85/:108/:121-127), which never runs; the song parks in _pending (music.js:118-124) and every retry hits a null ctx. DFU's enableVideos gates ONLY the VidPlayer push (DaggerfallUI.cs:1711-1713); the title song plays regardless (SetupGameWizard.cs:89/:176).
findings.consequence: A classic-skin player with the launcher off using ?novideo (documented as DFU's enableVideos, main.js:137) gets a silent title screen and menu; the armed 5STRONG.HMI survives into the game and can start over the director's track on the first in-game gesture.

findings.title: Duplicate payload keys make the 'tails were never shipped' fix inert
findings.claim: The single payload object literal (lines 535-565) declares `tail` and `tailCat` twice: the audit-annotated fix at lines 543-545 ('THE TAILS WERE NEVER SHIPPED') builds the argonian tail from ARGONIAN_HIDE, but the same literal re-declares `tail: packPiece(buildTail(ramps.skin,'argonian'))` and `tailCat` at line 565; the later duplicates win under JS object-literal semantics, so the line-544 ARGONIAN_HIDE build is computed and thrown away and the shipped argonian tail pack is colored with the human skin ramp.

findings.title: Silenced touch-caster re-arms melee timer: reset happens before the silence gate
findings.claim: DFU DoTouchSpell resets the melee timer only after its whole condition passes, ending with SetReadySpell (EnemyMotor.cs:621-628), which returns false when silenced (EntityEffectManager.cs:315 SilenceCheck) - a silenced enemy's DoTouchSpell fails without touching MeleeTimer and its ordinary melee fires normally. The port's EnemyCaster.update resets attack.meleeTimer (enemyCasting.js:114) BEFORE returning the touch decision; the silence gate runs later in castEnemySpell (:159) and returns false with the timer already re-armed 1.5-3s. The arm re-fires every time the timer hits 0, usually beating the melee decision (which needs a classic tick plus the DFRandom roll on that exact frame).
findings.consequence: Silence a touch-casting enemy (ghost, Frost Daedra, healer) and in the port it stands in melee range mostly not attacking - its melee timer perpetually re-armed by failed casts - where DFU's silenced caster falls back to normal melee attacks.

findings.title: Bow shots always use RangedAttack1 records; HasRangedAttack2 mobiles should use records 25-29
findings.claim: DFU picks the bow state: RangedAttack1 only if (HasRangedAttack1 && !HasRangedAttack2), else RangedAttack2 (EnemyMotor.cs:594-597); GetStateAnims maps RangedAttack2 to RangedAttack2Anims records 25-29 (DaggerfallMobileUnit.cs:840-841; EnemyBasics.cs:103-113). The port has a single 'ranged' state always returning RANGED_ATTACK1_ANIMS records 20-24 (mobileUnit.js:120), and hosts key one rangedStriking flag. Rows 130 (Battlemage) and 133 (Nightblade) carry hasRangedAttack2:true plus castsMagic (enemyBasics.js:2103, :2293), so hasBowAttack is true and their bow shots draw records 20-24 - which for these hasSpellAnimation rows are the SPELL-casting records.
findings.consequence: A Battlemage or Nightblade shooting its bow renders its spell-casting sprite animation instead of its bow animation (archive 489/490 records 20-24 vs 25-29); the arrow still fires on the -1 marker.

findings.title: Bow-band shots and spell casts not suppressed during knockback (CanAct chain incomplete)
findings.claim: DFU KnockbackMovement sets CanAct=false while KnockbackSpeed>0 (EnemyMotor.cs:317) and TakeAction runs only under `if (CanAct)` (:171-172), so DoRangedAttack (:469 - the 1/32 bow and 1/40 spell rolls) and DoTouchSpell (:473) never run mid-knockback; the Hurt state also counts as IsPlayingOneShot (Base/MobileUnit.cs:153-168), blocking the rolls at :587. The port models only the giveUpTimer part of CanAct: the band arm (enemyAttack.js:127-134) and both EnemyCaster branches (enemyCasting.js:110-130) keep running while ai.knockbackSpeed>0; hosts gate only paralysis/hostility (dungeonContext.js:2290/2312, exteriorFoes.js:294/299). Melee correctly keeps running (CanAct-independent in DFU).
findings.consequence: For the ~0.2-0.5s knockback window after each solid player hit, a port archer can loose its 1/32 bow shot and a caster can cast touch/ranged spells; DFU enemies cannot act at all during knockback - ranged foes fight back through hit-stun.

findings.title: Detour override reordered ahead of DoRangedAttack in the decision chain
findings.claim: DFU TakeAction calls DoRangedAttack at :469 and DoTouchSpell at :473 BEFORE the `if (avoidObstaclesTimer > 0) AttemptMove(...)` detour arm at :481-484, so an in-band shooter with sight+detection stands off and shoots even while a detour timer runs (the timer just decays). The port's _classicTick takes the detour arm first (enemyMotor.js:943-951) and only then calls _doRangedAttack (:956); its comment miscites :480-484 as "TakeAction's FIRST branch". test/audit24_wave35.test.js:113-114 pins this ordering ("the detour override first of all") - the pin restates the port, not the C#, which puts the detour after both attack calls.
findings.consequence: For up to 0.75s after an obstacle/fall probe fires, an archer or ranged caster inside the 6-51.2 band with the target in sight keeps walking its detour instead of standing off as DFU does; shots still roll from the attack component, so it shoots on the move.

findings.title: searchMult not reset when GiveUpTimer expires (or while pacified)
findings.claim: DFU HandleNoAction resets searchMult=0 on ANY of its three arms - target null, GiveUpTimer <= 0, or PredictedTargetPos sentinel (EnemyMotor.cs:357-366, searchMult=0 at :362) - every FixedUpdate. The port resets it only on the predictedTargetPos===null arm (enemyMotor.js:935); the gave-up arm at :931 (`!detected && giveUpTimer <= 0`) returns without touching searchMult, and a pacified foe skips _classicTick entirely (:1039) so no arm runs. The stale ramp is only cleared later by _getDestination's clear-path arm (:869).
findings.consequence: A foe that ramped its search (searchMult up to 10) then gave up resumes a later non-clear-path pursuit aiming up to 10 units past the last-known position instead of at it, walking somewhere DFU's freshly-reset foe would not.

findings.title: Touch casts gated on the attack machine being Idle; DFU DoTouchSpell has no one-shot gate
findings.claim: DFU's DoTouchSpell condition (EnemyMotor.cs:621-623) has no isPlayingOneShot term; the only one-shot early-out above it in TakeAction is OneShotPauseActionsWhilePlaying (:465), true only for SeducerTransform states (Base/MobileUnit.cs:174-184). So a DFU foe whose melee timer is 0 mid-swing casts the touch spell, ChangeEnemyState(Spell) cutting the swing. The port adds `idle` (attack.machine.state === 'Idle') to the touch arm (enemyCasting.js:107, :110), skipping the cast until the swing ends. Reachable when ResetMeleeTimer floors to 0: 1500 - 50*(level-10) + 450*(reflexes-2) <= 0, i.e. player level ~22+ at low reflexes, ~40 at average.
findings.consequence: Against high-level players, a touch-caster in melee range delays its cast by up to a full swing (~0.5-1s) and its interrupted melee blow lands where DFU would have cancelled it into the spell.

findings.title: GiveUpTimer frozen during paralysis/knockback; DFU UpdateTimers runs before the CanAct gate
findings.claim: DFU UpdateTimers runs unconditionally every FixedUpdate, before `if (CanAct) TakeAction` (EnemyMotor.cs:170-172): detection refills GiveUpTimer to 200 (:419-420) and it decrements per classic tick while undetected (:423-424) even for a paralyzed or knocked-back foe (HandleParalysis/KnockbackMovement only clear CanAct). The port's refill/decrement lives inside _classicTick (enemyMotor.js:929-930), which is skipped while paralyzed or knocked (:1039 `if (!paralyzed && !knocked && this.isHostile)`), so the timer freezes for the whole paralysis.
findings.consequence: A paralyzed foe whose player hides does not run down its 12.5s give-up window during the paralysis; when it wakes it resumes blind pursuit where DFU's foe would already have given up and stopped.

DFU: SetRuntimeData sets npcData.nameBank = GetNameBankOfCurrentRegion() (StaticNPC.cs:309, always Breton/Redguard) and GetDisplayName calls FullName(npcData.nameBank, gender) (:325-326); TalkManager.cs:2848 uses the region bank too; nothing assigns a race bank. findings.title: IsChildNPCData is unported; isChildNPC is read in three places and written nowhere
findings.claim: DFU StaticNPC.IsChildNPCData (:342-350) flags children by IsChildNPCTexture(archive, record) or factionID == 514, gating quest offers (TalkManager.cs:755-770) and the work pool (:2842). The port has no equivalent: grep of src/ shows isChildNPC/isChild only read (worldModes.js:979,1366 pass !!pn.isChildNPC; npcSession.js:466,653) and never written, and staticNpc.js carries neither the 514 constant nor the child texture table. The flag is constant false.

findings.title: Billboard anim frame not reset to 0 on idle/move state switch
findings.claim: DFU MobilePersonBillboard.SetIdle (:291-313) resets currentFrame = 0 and animTimer = 1 on every idle<->move transition, so each state starts at frame 0. The port's MobilePerson.update (mobilePerson.js:245-256) keeps one monotonically increasing this.frame and this._timer across state changes and takes frame % n, so a transition starts at an arbitrary phase of the new record's cycle.
findings.consequence: A townsperson stopping to face the player (or resuming walking) starts the idle/walk cycle at a random frame instead of frame 0 - a small visible animation-phase divergence.

findings.title: place() marks the spawn tile Occupied; DFU never flags a spawn tile

findings.title: Jump gate misses the WasClimbing bypass; climbing.js wasClimbing is computed and never read
findings.claim: AcrobatMotor.HandleJumpInput:76 gates the jump with `if (!climbingMotor.WasClimbing && playerMotor.GroundedTime < 0.1f) return;` - a player who was climbing at the start of this frame's check may jump with zero grounded time. The port's gate (motor.js:649) is `this.grounded && input.jump && this.groundedTime >= GROUNDED_JUMP_GATE_S && !this.slowFalling` with no climbing bypass. The port DOES track the flag - climbing.js:119 writes `this.wasClimbing = this.isClimbing` every step - but grep of src/ shows no reader anywhere: a ported member with no caller.
findings.consequence: Topping out or aborting a climb onto ground then pressing Jump: DFU jumps instantly, the port refuses the jump for the next 0.1 s of grounded time.

findings.title: Over-encumbered swimmer forced sink missing from the swim path
findings.claim: LevitateMotor.Update:83-85: `overEncumbered = (CarriedWeight * 4 > 250) && !playerLevitating && !GodMode; if (playerSwimming && overEncumbered && !climbingMotor.IsClimbing && !IsWaterWalking) upDownVector += Vector3.down; else if (Jump/FloatUp)...` - the sink REPLACES the float keys, so an over-encumbered swimmer is pushed down every frame and cannot float up. The port's swim path (motor.js:530-531) reads only `input.up`/`input.down` from the host's keys; no host or motor code computes carried weight for the swim path (grep for encumb/CarriedWeight in src/scenes and src/player finds none feeding the motor).
findings.consequence: Carrying more than 62.5 kg while swimming: DFU drags the player to the bottom and blocks surfacing; the port swims and surfaces freely regardless of load.

findings.title: Crouch stays live while levitating; no forced stand for a crouched levitator
findings.claim: DFU DecideHeightAction: while levitating a crouched player is forced to DoStanding (PlayerHeightChanger.cs:137-145), and the crouch-press block is nested under `else if (!riding && !onWater && !levitating)` (:171), so the Crouch press does nothing while levitating. The port's _heightAction first arm (motor.js:358) is `input.crouch && (!this.swimming || this.grounded)` with no levitating term and no forced-stand arm, so the crouch toggle fires while levitating and a crouched player who starts levitating stays crouched.
findings.consequence: In the port a levitating player can toggle the 0.9 crouch capsule mid-air (fitting through gaps DFU forbids) and a crouched levitator keeps crouch speed/eye; DFU forces standing and ignores the key.

findings.title: Climbing does not force a crouched player to stand
findings.claim: DFU DecideHeightAction's second arm in the on-foot block: `else if (climbing) { timerMax = timerMedium; if (crouching) heightAction = DoStanding; forcedSwimCrouch = false; }` (PlayerHeightChanger.cs:184-191) - climbing forces the standing capsule every frame. The port's _heightAction (motor.js:352-368) has only the crouch-press, swim-force, and swim-unforce arms; nothing reads the climb state, and ClimbingState.step/_climbStep have no crouch gate, so a crouched player climbs crouched and remains crouched after topping out.
findings.consequence: A crouched climber in the port keeps the 0.9 capsule and crouched eye through and after the climb (and can climb under 0.9-1.8 clearances); DFU stands the player up on the medium (0.25 s) clock as the climb starts.

findings.title: Outdoor hosts pass no pitch and no up/down: levitation above ground cannot change height
findings.claim: LevitateMotor.Update:71-91 moves along the camera look (pitch included) and reads Jump/FloatUp for up, Crouch/FloatDown for down - everywhere. The motor implements this (motor.js:520-531; contract at :299-301) and the dungeon hosts wire it (dungeon.js:400-403 and worldModes.js:2660-2663 pass up/down and cam.pitch). But both outdoor hosts call player.update with only {forward, strafe, run, sneak, jump, crouch} and cam.yaw - no up/down, no pitch (exterior.js:1482-1489; world.js:3135-3142) - while shared.js:382 sets player.levitating outdoors each frame. With pitch defaulting 0 and up/down undefined, my is always 0 in the levitate branch and velY is forced 0.
findings.consequence: Cast Levitate outdoors (spell 14,255 exists in the port): the player hovers frozen at current height - no key and no look direction can ascend or descend until the effect expires. In DFU levitation works identically indoors and out.

findings.title: Crouch key does not drive float-down while swimming/levitating in any host
findings.claim: LevitateMotor.Update:86-89: `else if (HasAction(Jump) || HasAction(FloatUp)) up; else if (HasAction(Crouch) || HasAction(FloatDown)) down;` - the held Crouch key dives a swimmer and descends a levitator. The motor's own contract states this (motor.js:300: 'up/down: the Jump/FloatUp and Crouch/FloatDown keys, HELD'), but every host maps only FloatDown: dungeon.js:401 and worldModes.js:2661 both pass `down: held(keys, 'FloatDown')`, and the outdoor hosts pass nothing. The hosts' up arm does match (jumpHeld || FloatUp).
findings.consequence: Holding Crouch (C) while swimming does nothing in the port (only PageDown dives); in DFU it dives. Combined with the missing levitate gate in _heightAction, Crouch while levitating toggles the stance instead of descending.

findings.title: Slowfall constant velocity is fixed-rate-coupled: 1.75 m/s vs DFU's 2.1 m/s
findings.claim: AcrobatMotor.ApplyGravity:187 sets `moveDirection.y = -slowFallSpeed * Time.deltaTime` in FixedUpdate, i.e. a fall VELOCITY of 105 * fixedDeltaTime; DFU's ProjectSettings/TimeManager.asset:6 pins Fixed Timestep 0.02, so DFU slowfalls at 2.1 m/s. The port copies the shape verbatim (motor.js:670 `velY = -SLOWFALL_SPEED * dt`) but steps at FIXED_DT = 1/60 (motor.js:73), giving 1.75 m/s. The 60 Hz step is a documented port choice, but slowfall is the one law whose observable magnitude changes with that rate, and the pin motorStairs.test.js:295 asserts -105/60, restating the port without noting DFU's 0.02.
findings.consequence: Slow Falling descents are ~17% slower than DFU (2.1 -> 1.75 m/s); timing-sensitive drops under the buff take 20% longer. Fall damage is unaffected (slowfall re-anchors fallStart each tick in both).

findings.claim: frame() calls player.update every modal frame, with zeroed inputs when overlayHeld (worldModes.js:2654) - gravity, velocity and the crouch input (`crouch: crouchHeld && !latch.crouch` in the held arm) keep running under a window. dungeon.js gates the whole motor behind `if (walkMode && !overlayHeld)` (dungeon.js:353-357, 'no movers, no motor'). DFU pauses the game for any PauseWhileOpen window (UserInterfaceManager.cs:179-184 AddWindow -> PauseGame(true)), which worldModes' own comment (:2631-2634) cites as the law. Zeroed inputs are right for paralysis only.
findings.consequence: Open a window mid-fall in a world-hosted interior/dungeon: the fall completes under the paused menu and fall damage lands (applyFallLanding :2708); a swimmer keeps sinking; the crouch key toggles crouch under a window. The standalone host and DFU both freeze.

findings.title: Shelves in a broken-into CLOSED shop open the Buy trade window; DFU opens the stealing inventory
findings.claim: DFU gates shelf activation on IsPlayerInsideOpenShop (PlayerActivate.cs:887-899): open -> Buy trade window; closed -> InventoryWindow.SetShopShelfStealing. The port computes insideOpenShop at the door (worldModes.js:2205-2207, PlayerActivate.cs:1120 verbatim) but feeds it only to the people gate and drops it; openShelf (:634-647) checks only isShop and always stocks + opens the Buy window. A closed shop is enterable via the steal-mode lockpick ladder (:2167-2188). The shoplifting FORMULA is a recorded pending (crime arc), but DFU never opens a paying trade window in a closed shop regardless.
findings.consequence: Break into a shop at night in Steal mode and the empty shop SELLS to you at full price where DFU gives the shoplifting inventory; the computed open-shop latch is dead after entry.

findings.title: Identify-SPELL commit tallies Mercantile and skips DFU's not-enough-magicka refusal
findings.claim: commitTrade runs tallySkill(Mercantile, 1) unconditionally after every mode (worldModes.js:785), including the identifySpell arm (:772-779). DFU's identify-spell pass runs inside DoModeAction (DaggerfallTradeWindow.cs:957-995) and never reaches ConfirmTrade's TallySkill at :1088 - no tally for the spell (the paid service does tally, and the port matches there). DFU also refuses the whole pass when IdentifySpellCost > CurrentMagicka (:960-963); the port has no gate anywhere in the chain - commitTrade clamps Math.max(0, magicka - cost) (:775-777) and identifies everything anyway.
findings.consequence: Every Identify cast trains Mercantile (accumulating skill-progress divergence), and a cast concluded with insufficient magicka still identifies all staged items where DFU refuses.

findings.title: Quest ITEM stands take the NPC placement law; DFU's AddQuestItem never ground-rays
findings.claim: standQuestFlatIn applies one law to NPCs and items: dungeon anchor `y - size.h/2` (the ITEM's own half-height) plus the AlignBillboardToGround raycast (worldModes.js:464-466); its comment asserts AddQuestNPC/AddQuestItem 'both call' the align (:457-459). AddQuestItem (GameObjectHelper.cs:1116-1160) never calls AlignBillboardToGround: its dungeon shift is the CONSTANT -randomTreasureMarkerDim/2 * GlobalScale = -0.5 (:1135-1136; DaggerfallLoot.cs:33, dim=40), then +Size.y/2, and the position stands with no ray. Only AddQuestNPC rays (:1040). standItem routes items through the same path with no distinction (worldModes.js:508-513, :576-580).
findings.consequence: A dungeon quest item whose world-sprite height differs from 1.0 unit sits at a different height than DFU, and an item on an elevated marker (table, cage, ledge) is ray-snapped down to the surface below where DFU leaves it at the marker.

findings.title: Quest-NPC ground ray originates at the BOTTOM anchor + 0.2; DFU rays from the CENTRE + 0.2
findings.claim: AlignBillboardToGround casts from go.transform.position + 0.2 (GameObjectHelper.cs:340), and at that moment the position is the billboard CENTRE (interior: marker + Size.y/2 per :1034-1037; dungeon: the marker itself). The port rays from its bottom anchor `by + 0.2` (worldModes.js:465), half a sprite height LOWER in both site types. The on-hit landing formula agrees (bottom = hit + 0.02h), but the origin difference changes which floors the 4-unit ray finds: in a dungeon the port's origin (marker - h/2 + 0.2) can start at or below the floor for tall sprites.
findings.consequence: Edge geometry only: a tall-sprite dungeon quest NPC can miss the floor snap DFU performs and stand embedded; floors near the 4-unit limit are found by one side and not the other.

findings.title: commitTrade's 'Repair' arm has no caller and skips the UpdateRepairTimes queue law
findings.claim: No call site opens the native trade window in 'Repair' mode (openTradeWindow is called with Buy/Sell/Identify/SellMagic only; openRepairService uses the keyed ChoiceWindow flow) - the arm at worldModes.js:755-765 is dead. If wired it diverges from DFU's ConfirmTrade Repair arm (DaggerfallTradeWindow.cs:1060-1072 -> UpdateRepairTimes(true) :514-568): it calls leaveForRepair with a bare per-item calculateItemRepairTime - no longest-job stretch, no never-decrease clamp - which the port's own keyed repairItem applies via updateRepairTimes (worldModes.js:1975-1984); its InstantRepairs branch also addItem()s an item never removed from the pack.
findings.consequence: None reachable today (dead arm); a future wiring of the INVE12 native repair mode would silently skip the repair-queue law and duplicate instantly-repaired items.

findings.title: bypassSavingThrows wrongly suppresses the magnitude-scaling saving throw
findings.claim: Port: `saveScaled = spell.rangeType !== 0 && !ctx.bypassSavingThrows` gates effectMagnitude's savingThrow scaling (effects.js:437-441,577). DFU: AssignBundleFlags.BypassSavingThrows gates only the assign-time no-magnitude save (EntityEffectManager.cs:565-568) and reflection/resistance (:521,:525); GetMagnitude's ModifyEffectAmount runs for every non-CasterOnly bundle regardless of the flag (EntityEffect.cs:804-806), so bypassed casts of magnitude effects are still save-scaled per application in DFU. Reachable: quest spell-queue casts on foes - QuestResourceBehaviour.cs:346 assigns with BypassSavingThrows and the port mirrors it at questFoeHost.js:91 with bypassSavingThrows:true.
findings.consequence: A quest-queued magnitude spell (Damage Health, Continuous Damage) lands at full magnitude every round in the port where DFU scales it by the foe's saving throw - quest foes take measurably more damage.

findings.title: Soul Trap never rolls the target's no-magnitude saving throw
findings.claim: DFU AssignBundle rolls FormulaHelper.SavingThrow for any effect with SupportMagnitude=false on a non-CasterOnly cast, dropping the whole effect on a full save (EEM:565-579). SoulTrap has SupportChance+SupportDuration, no magnitude, TargetFlags_Other, and does not set bypassSavingThrows (SoulTrap.cs:30-41; the bypass field's only writers are vampirism/lycanthropy/special effects). The port's soul-trap arm (effects.js:1278-1295) checks mobileType and rounds, then pushes/stacks with no savingThrow call - only the cast chance is forced true, which matches ChanceSuccess.
findings.consequence: A monster with high willpower or Magic tolerance can never shrug off Soul Trap in the port; in DFU a full save drops the trap entirely - traps land strictly more often.

findings.title: Pacify and Charm skip the no-magnitude saving throw
findings.claim: PacifyEffect (SupportChance, no magnitude, TargetFlags_Other, PacifyEffect.cs:60-63) and CharmEffect (CharmEffect.cs:33-44) go through DFU's AssignBundle no-magnitude save (EEM:565-579) after the OnCast chance gate - the target can fully save and drop the effect. The port's arm (effects.js:1207-1216) does the group/class match and the dice100 chance roll only; no savingThrow is ever rolled for these kinds.
findings.consequence: Pacify/Charm succeed more often in the port than in DFU against targets with Magic tolerance or high willpower - chance is the only gate instead of chance AND save.

findings.title: Paralyze hard-immunity gate runs after reflection instead of before it
findings.claim: DFU drops an incoming Paralyze for a hard-immune entity BEFORE the absorption/reflection/resistance chain (EEM:495-498 continue precedes the caster block at :504-527). The port tests isEntityImmuneToParalysis inside the isParalyze arm (effects.js:935), which runs AFTER the reflection gate (:672-679) and resistance gate (:685-691), so a hard-immune target with live Spell Reflection reflects a pure-Paralyze bundle back at the caster (out.reflected, re-applied by hosts at hostMagic.js:124-131 and world.js:1223-1225) where DFU silently discards the effect.
findings.consequence: A player under Free Action (or a paralysis-immune career/race) with Spell Reflection up bounces a spider/wraith paralyze back at its caster; in DFU nothing happens. The resistance gate can also print 'Spell was resisted.' where DFU is silent.

findings.title: Caster concealment break missing on Transfer/Drain/Paralyze/Silence arms
findings.claim: DFU runs HandleAttackFromSource on the caster for these effects: TransferHealth/TransferFatigue via DamageHealthFromSource/DamageFatigueFromSource (DaggerfallEntityBehaviour.cs:143-169), and DrainEffect (:57), TransferEffect, Paralyze, Silence, DamageSpellPoints via PlayerAggro (EntityEffect.cs:815-828 -> HandleAttackFromSource :196-200), which breaks the caster's normal-power concealment. The port calls handleAttackFromSource only in the damageHealth/damageFatigue/damageSpellPoints/continuous arms; the transferHealth (effects.js:828-841), transferFatigue (:843-856), drain/transfer-attribute (:786-817), paralyze (:929-960) and buff/silence (:1297-1329) arms never call it.
findings.consequence: An invisibility-normal or chameleon-normal player casting Paralyze, Silence, Transfer Health/Fatigue or a Drain at a foe keeps their concealment in the port; DFU breaks it when the cast lands.

findings.title: seedBundleSeq has no caller - restored bundleIds collide with new casts
findings.claim: effects.js:194-195 exports seedBundleSeq to lift the module-scope _bundleSeq past a restored save's high water mark, but grep of src/ finds zero callers. save.js persists bundleId (copyEffectEntry spreads whole entries, save.js:74-89, snapshot :155) and restores them (:303) without seeding, so after an app restart + load, _bundleSeq is 0 and the next cast reuses bundleId 1, colliding with the restored first cast's entries. liveBundles (mysticism.js:231-248) then merges two casts into one bundle and dispelBundle (mysticism.js:261-270, consumed at worldModes.js:3762) removes both. DFU has no counter to collide - bundles are object references re-instanced on load.
findings.consequence: Cast a buff, save, restart the app, load, cast another spell: the HUD spell icons merge into one row and Dispel Magic on it strips both casts at once.

findings.title: soulTrapNameSuffix is a ported function with no caller
findings.claim: mysticism.js:379-385 ports ItemHelper.ResolveItemLongName's filled-trap suffix ('Soul Trap (Wraith)'), but grep of src/ finds no caller outside mysticism.js itself - no naming path appends it; only the info panel's %hs macro (itemInfo.js:190) surfaces the trapped soul.
findings.consequence: A filled soul trap's item name never shows which soul it holds anywhere its name is printed; the player must open the info panel to tell full traps apart.

findings.title: 'You are regenerating.' and 'You feel drained.' HUD lines never emitted
findings.claim: DFU's Regenerate.Start prints youAreRegenerating for a player host (Regenerate.cs:48-52) and DrainEffect prints youFeelDrained on each magnitude increase when the host is the player (DrainEffect.cs:102-106); both strings verified in Internal_Strings.csv:638/642. The port's regenerate arm (effects.js:916-928) and drain/transfer arm (:786-817) call no sinks.say, and grep of src/ finds neither string anywhere, while the sibling concealment start texts and 'Spell was absorbed.' are wired.
findings.consequence: The player gets no HUD feedback when a Regenerate lands on them or when a drain saps a stat, unlike DFU.

findings.title: Create Item lastSelectedIndex is per-host instead of one static
findings.claim: DFU's CreateItem.lastSelectedIndex is a single static shared across all casts in a run (CreateItem.cs:29,75,121). The port keeps two independent module-level copies - worldModes.js:189 and dungeonContext.js:137 - so the picker's remembered row does not carry between a dungeon cast and an overworld/interior cast.
findings.consequence: Cast Create Item in a dungeon picking row N, exit, cast again outside: the picker opens at the exterior host's own remembered row (initially 0) instead of row N.

findings.title: Dungeon water footstep hysteresis dropped: single 0.57 threshold vs DFU 0.57-enter/0.95-exit
findings.claim: DFU enters shallow-water footsteps when (transform.y - 0.57) < waterY (PlayerFootsteps.cs:189) but resets water footsteps to stone only when (transform.y - 0.95) >= waterY or the water level clears (:199-208); between the thresholds the current water sound sticks. The port's pickFootstepSet is stateless (footsteps.js:49-50) and both dungeon hosts recompute dungeonShallow each frame with only the enter threshold (dungeon.js:414, worldModes.js:2679: (player.pos[1] + 0.9 - 0.57) < surf), so the port flips to stone 0.38 units earlier than DFU; same on leaving the submerged/swimming state.

findings.claim: DFU: amount = 11; if (climbingMotor.IsClimbing) amount = ClimbingFatigueLoss (22); else if running 88; else if swimming... (PlayerEntity.cs:405-413, constants :109-113). findings.title: resetMagicRoundMarker never called: forward load fires up to 2880 spurious magic rounds
findings.claim: DFU resets the broker's lastGameMinute on start AND load (InitMagicRoundTimer :817-823 'Called when game starts or loaded', plus LoadInProgress :206). The port's resetMagicRoundMarker (worldTick.js:608) has NO caller in src/. claimMagicRounds re-anchors only when the clock moved BACKWARDS (worldTick.js:119); its comment claims save.js re-anchors explicitly, but save.js:408 re-anchors only entity.lastGameMinutes, not the broker marker. worldQuickLoad (world.js:1654) sets the clock in-session with no marker reset, so a load to a LATER game time yields from = max(marker, to-2880) and a burst of up to 2880 rounds.
findings.consequence: Loading a save ahead of the session clock instantly runs up to 2880 magic rounds: restored buffs expire on the spot, poisons burst, and a restored continuous-damage effect can kill on load.

findings.title: 8-hour enemy-alert decay never runs in the dungeon hosts
findings.claim: DFU lowers the alert 8 hours after raise inside PlayerEntity.Update (:381-384), every context. The port's decayEnemyAlert has ONE call site, createPlayerTicker.tick (shared.js:746) - pinned to exactly one by test/audit24_wave36.test.js:122-126 - but both dungeon hosts drive the clock via dungeonCtx.drawFoes -> tickPlayerMinutes directly (dungeonContext.js:2100; called from worldModes.js:2764 and dungeon.js:475), never through createPlayerTicker, and tickPlayerMinutes contains no decay. In a dungeon the alert clears only when a detecting foe dies (dungeonContext.js:1847).
findings.consequence: Once any dungeon foe sees the player, the alert stays raised for the visit: the resting random-spawn roll keeps the alerted higher rate forever, where DFU relaxes it after 8 game hours.

findings.title: NPCSession's mobile arm has no caller; walker talk never sets the session target
findings.claim: TalkManager.TalkToMobileNPC (:726-744) sets the mobile target: npcData rebuilt as Commoners of the region, alreadyRejectedOnce reset, numAnswersGivenTellMeAboutOrRumors zeroed. The port ports the arm (npcSession.js:439-455, :357-383) but nothing calls it: only talkToStaticNPC has callers (worldModes.js:978, :1365); the walker click runs townTalk.js's local path (:300-329) which never sets the session target. answerPipeline._session() (answerPipeline.js:289) reads npcSession.npcData for socialGroup/counters, so a walker conversation serves whatever the LAST static NPC left there.

findings.title: Cure-disease price skips the regional price adjustment DFU always applies
findings.claim: DFU computes costBeforeBargaining = FormulaHelper.CalculateCost(baseCost, quality) (cs:85), and CalculateCost unconditionally runs ApplyRegionalPriceAdjustment (FormulaHelper.cs:1895, 2026-2044), scaling by the region's PriceAdjustment (750-1250). The port calls calculateCost(baseCost, quality) (guildServiceActions.js:215) whose third priceAdjustment parameter defaults to neutral 1000 (shopStock.js:325-328); the comment misreads the two-arg C# call - the omitted third parameter is conditionPercentage, not the regional term. The port models regional prices elsewhere (tradeModes.js:242) but never passes them here.
findings.consequence: Temple curing costs the same in every province; in DFU the quote varies up to about +/-25% with the region's price adjustment.

findings.title: Knightly rank-9 promotion never consults house ownership; blocking flag is stale

findings.title: Non-member at knightly seneschal gets rank refusal 460 instead of members-only line

findings.consequence: Any non-member clicking a knightly order seneschal sees the rank-9 refusal text instead of DFU's members-only line - reachable, player-visible wrong message.

findings.title: Stendarr AvoidDeath benefit missing entirely - no port counterpart, no flag

findings.title: ItemDeteriorates params shifted: DFU 0=AllTheTime/1=Sunlight/2=Holy, port 0=sunlight/1=holy/2=always
findings.claim: DFU's Params enum is AllTheTime=0, InSunlight=1, InHolyPlaces=2, and MagicRound returns early only when (param==InSunlight && !inSunlight) || (param==InHolyPlaces && !inHolyPlace) — param 0 degrades unconditionally. The port's magicRound gates `param === 0` on ctx.inSunlight and `param === 1` on ctx.inHolyPlace, so param 2 falls through both ifs and degrades unconditionally. The port's own catalogue (enchantmentCatalogue.js:80,251,259) uses the correct DFU order (labels 0='all the time', 1='in sunlight', 2='in holy places'; Daedroth/FrostDaedra/Ghost/Wraith souls force param 2 = InHolyPlaces), so the two port modules disagree with each other as well as with the C#.
findings.consequence: A soul-bound item carrying ItemDeteriorates InHolyPlaces (param 2) loses 1 condition every 4 magic rounds everywhere and is eventually consumed; an all-the-time (param 0) drawback never fires; sunlight (param 1) items idle on the holy-place seam.

findings.title: HealthLeech params shifted: DFU 0=WheneverUsed/1=Daily/2=Weekly, port 2=WheneverUsed/0=Daily/1=Weekly
findings.claim: DFU's Params enum is WheneverUsed=0, UnlessUsedDaily=1, UnlessUsedWeekly=2: the use/strike bill (16/8 hp) fires at param 0 (:86), the idle drain at params 1 (day) and 2 (week). The port's used/strikes handlers bill at `param === 2` and its magicRound treats 0 as daily and 1 as weekly. The catalogue (enchantmentCatalogue.js:77,253: labels 0='Whenever used', DaedraSeducer forces param 2 = UnlessUsedWeekly) uses the correct DFU order, so port modules also disagree with each other. test/enchantments.test.js:62 (`item(T.HealthLeech, 2) // WheneverUsed`) and :103 (param 0 as daily) pin the port's wrong mapping while citing HealthLeech.cs — the pin restates the port.
findings.consequence: A Daedra-Seducer-bound item (weekly leech in DFU) bills the wearer 16 hp per use / 8 per strike; a classic WheneverUsed (param 0) item instead drains 1 hp per 4 rounds after a day idle and never bills on use.

findings.title: Enchanted payload never dispatched: FeatherWeight/ExtraWeight/HealthLeech maker arms are dead code
findings.claim: DFU's SetEnchantments fires EnchantmentPayloadCallback(Enchanted) per enchantment carrying the flag (:1298-1300) and unequips the item (:1341). The port's applyEnchantments (enchanting.js:200-206) only copies the list, ui/itemMakerWindow.js:285 calls it with no payload dispatch, and no caller anywhere in src/ passes PAYLOAD.Enchanted to doItemEnchantmentPayloads — the registry's enchanted() handlers (enchantments.js:424-425) and HealthLeech's Enchanted stamp arm can never run, and SoulBound's trap consumption has no path either.
findings.consequence: Feather Weight leaves the item's weight unchanged (DFU sets 0.25kg); Extra Weight never quadruples it; a fresh daily/weekly HealthLeech item starts at stamp 0 and leeches immediately; the item stays equipped where DFU force-unequips.

findings.title: Recipe picker part-fills the cauldron; DFU refuses on any missing ingredient and clears first
findings.claim: DFU's AddRecipeToCauldron builds a dict of required ingredients and, if ANY is unmatched, shows 'reqIngredients' and moves NOTHING (:298-300); only with all present does it ClearCauldron() (:304) then add the full set. The port's gatherRecipe comment claims DFU 'fills what it can... does not refuse the whole recipe for one missing herb', and the caller (ui/potionMakerWindow.js:184-194) adds the found subset on top of existing cauldron contents with no message and no clear. test/potions.test.js:179-188 pins the partial fill while citing the same C# lines — the pin restates the port, not the C#.
findings.consequence: Picking a known recipe while missing one herb silently loads a partial cauldron; Mix then fails and consumes the herbs where DFU would have refused with a message and consumed nothing. Residual cauldron contents also pollute a fill instead of being cleared.

findings.title: WeakensArmor applies +5 armor in port but is a no-op in DFU (setter guard refuses positive values)
findings.claim: WeakensArmor's ConstantEffect calls SetDecreasedArmorValueModifier(5), but that setter (DaggerfallEntity.cs:410-416) assigns only when `amount < DecreasedArmorValueModifier`, and the modifier is cleared to 0 every DoConstantEffects pass (ClearConstantEffects, DaggerfallEntity.cs:842) — 5 < 0 is never true, so the +5 never lands and the enchantment is inert in DFU. The port's row adds WEAKENS_ARMOR_VALUE (+5) into mods.armorMod each round, which combat/formulas.js:292 adds to the wearer's armor value in the attacker's hit chance.
findings.consequence: In the port a WeakensArmor side effect makes the wearer 5 points easier to hit; in DFU it does nothing — the drawback the player took for -700 budget costs defense only in the port.

findings.title: Armor modifiers stack additively per item in port; DFU's setters are non-stacking min-sets
findings.claim: DFU's SetIncreasedArmorValueModifier keeps only the lowest value ('does not stack'), so any number of StrengthensArmor items (each setting -5 via StrengthensArmor.cs:63) yields exactly -5; BadReactionsFrom's SetDecreasedArmorValueModifier(-5) likewise floors at -5 across items (its ChanceToHitModifier IS additive, DaggerfallEntity.cs:418-421). The port folds these into one additive channel: each StrengthensArmor row does `mods.armorMod += -5` (enchantments.js:428) and each active BadReactionsFrom adds another -5 (:527), so two Strengthens items give -10 where DFU caps at -5.
findings.consequence: Wearing two or more StrengthensArmor items (or multiple active BadReactionsFrom items) makes the port player measurably harder to hit than DFU allows — -5 per item instead of a -5 channel cap.

findings.title: Enchantment cap off-by-one: DFU's `++count > 10` break applies 11, port slices at 10
findings.claim: SetEnchantments increments count AFTER adding each enchantment and breaks only when `++count > maxEnchantments` (10) — the break fires after the 11th add, so an oversized list keeps 11 enchantments. The port's applyEnchantments does `enchantments.slice(0, MAX_ENCHANTMENTS)` (10), and its comment says 'DFU applies the first ten'. The port's own openPickerDecision comment notes forced enchantments can push the lists past the ==10 picker guard, so 11+ lists are reachable.
findings.consequence: An 11-enchantment item (e.g. via SoulBound's forced children crossing the ==10 guard) silently loses its 11th enchantment in the port; DFU keeps it.

findings.title: Book arm lacks DFU's !IsArtifact guard
findings.claim: DFU's book arm is `item.ItemGroup == ItemGroups.Books && !item.IsArtifact` — artifact books (Oghma Infinium) skip the reader and fall through to the enchanted Used payload at the tail. The port's isBook (useItem.js:80) tests group only, so an artifact book answers {kind:'book'} and opens the reader before the payload.
findings.consequence: When artifact items exist in the port, using the Oghma Infinium opens the plain book reader instead of only firing its artifact payload; low reachability today since artifact effect classes pend.

findings.title: CastWhenHeld wear runs for non-player wearers; DFU's MagicRound payload is player-only
findings.claim: DFU dispatches the MagicRound item payload only for items in activeMagicItemsInRound, populated solely under `if (IsPlayerEntity)` (:1744-1752) — an enemy's Cast-When-Held item never takes the 1-per-4-rounds wear. The port's pump (worldTick.js:160, 'every host's player AND foes get it') calls enchantmentMagicRound for foes too, and CastWhenHeld's magicRound (enchantments.js:316-319) has no player gate, so an enemy's held item degrades and is consumed on break via enchantLowerCondition. (Bundle-driven rounds — RegensHealth, ItemDeteriorates, HealthLeech idle — do run for any entity in DFU, so those are correctly ungated.)
findings.consequence: An enemy wearing a Cast-When-Held magic item has it wear out and vanish over time in the port; in DFU it survives to be looted at its remaining condition.

findings.title: createArtifact never marks the artifact identified (DFU sets identifiedMask at mint)
findings.claim: DFU SetArtifact writes `flags = artifactMask | identifiedMask` (DaggerfallUnityItem.cs:617) so every artifact is born identified. The port's createArtifact (loot.js:280-295) sets artifact/magic/enchantments but never isIdentified, and no other producer does (only shopStock.js:484 and worldModes.js:774/782 write isIdentified). itemIsIdentified (tradeModes.js:130) requires isIdentified===true for any enchanted item, so every artifact reads UNIDENTIFIED.
findings.consequence: expandItemInfo (itemInfo.js:186-189) drops an unidentified item's own name, so an artifact's info panel shows the base template name instead of the artifact name; the Identify service stages an artifact and charges (25*value)>>8 (tradeModes.js:244-251, 363) where DFU refuses (DaggerfallTradeWindow.cs:823-826).

findings.title: Equip-swap pause billed per hand transition; DFU bills only the net change per inventory-window session
findings.claim: DFU snapshots the hand items at inventory OnPush (SetEquipDelayTime(false), DaggerfallInventoryWindow.cs:667) and bills once at OnPop (:729): only `if (lastRightHandItem != currentRightHandItem)` adds delay(last)+delay(current) (:1164-1183). The port's billEquipDelay (equip.js:52-58) fires inside unequipSlot (:67) and equipItem (:190) on EVERY transition; its comment claims 'each transition exactly once' is the DFU law. test/ch3.test.js:77 pins the accumulating behavior - the pin restates the port; its single-swap case happens to match DFU.
findings.consequence: Multiple equips in one inventory visit over-bill the attack-block countdown: dagger then katana from empty hands bills 500+500+3400 where DFU bills 3400; unequip and re-equip the same weapon bills 2x its delay where DFU bills zero. The weapon is blocked longer than classic after any multi-step swap.

findings.title: Alchemist shelf never rolls the 25% potion recipe though the ported helper ships in loot.js
findings.claim: DFU StockShopShelf's Alchemist arm calls RandomlyAddPotionRecipe(25, items) (DaggerfallLoot.cs:163-166). The port's Alchemist branch is a comment only (shopStock.js:150-152, 'potion recipes pend (loud)'), but the stated blocker no longer exists: loot.js:383-389 ships randomlyAddPotionRecipe verbatim (CLASSIC_RECIPE_KEYS, template 278), already consumed by addEnemyLootExtras (loot.js:404) and addPileLootExtras (loot.js:423), and shopStock.js already imports createRandomPotion from the same module (line 108).
findings.consequence: Alchemist shop shelves never stock a potion recipe (25% chance per restock in DFU/classic), removing the main legitimate purchase source of recipes.

findings.title: Shop shelves skip the MagicItems group; Pawn Shops never stock random magic items
findings.claim: DFU's shelf loop creates CreateRandomMagicItem for the MagicItems group (DaggerfallLoot.cs:240-243); itemGroupsPawnShop carries pair 0x04,0x0A (DaggerfallLootDataTables.cs:61) so pawn shops stock magic items at chanceMod 10. The port hard-skips: `if (group === 'MagicItems') continue; // INTERIM loud` (shopStock.js:166), yet the same file already mints real magic items via createRegularMagicItem for the guild shelf (shopStock.js:483) and loot.js exposes the MAGIC.DEF registry via getMagicItemTemplates() (loot.js:302).
findings.consequence: Pawn shop shelves never show a random enchanted item (in DFU each MagicItems template rolls Dice100 under 10*5*(21-rarity)/100 when rarity <= quality), closing a classic source of purchasable magic items.

findings.title: Repair days label uses committed time, not the queue-stretched estimate, for in-repair items
findings.claim: DFU's label calls item.RepairData.EstimatedDaysUntilRepaired() (DaggerfallTradeWindow.cs:283-288), reading timeStarted + EstimatedRepairTime (ItemRepairData.cs:36-42) - the value the estimate pass just recomputed with the longest-job stretch and never-decrease clamp (DaggerfallTradeWindow.cs:548, 556, 566). The port's repairStatusLabel (repairService.js:156-163) uses repairTimeDone(item) = timeStarted + committed repairTime for any in-repair item, ignoring its estimateMinutes parameter in that branch.
findings.consequence: When an in-repair item is the longest job and more items are staged beside it, DFU shows the new stretched estimate (e.g. '4 days') while the port shows the old committed '3 days' until the trade confirms - a transient label divergence.

findings.title: Forced (child) enchantment rows can be removed by clicking them
findings.claim: DFU's EnchantmentPanel_OnMouseClick only removes a panel when panel.Enchantment.ParentEnchantment == 0 ('child panels are removed by clicking on parent', EnchantmentListPicker.cs:268-271). The port's click handler (itemMakerWindow.js:338-344) hit-tests any visible row and calls _removeRow(hit.entry) with no parentEnchantment guard; removeEnchantment (enchantmentCatalogue.js:360-362) then filters the clicked entry out by its own key, so a forced child (which carries parentEnchantment = parent key and its own key) is removed on its own. findings.title: Enchanting a stacked item enchants the whole stack (no SplitStack)
findings.claim: DFU's EnchantButton_OnMouseClick splits one item off a stack before enchanting: 'if (selectedItem.IsAStack()) selectedItem = ...Items.SplitStack(selectedItem, 1)' (cs:752-754). The port's _enchant (itemMakerWindow.js:277-294) calls applyEnchantments(this.selected, ...) directly, and applyEnchantments (enchanting.js:200-206) just sets item.enchantments on the object - no stack split anywhere. Gems (Ingredients tab, itemMakerFilter line 120) are stackable in the port (inventory.js isStackable:110 - ingredients stack), so a merged stack of N gems is a single selectable item.
findings.consequence: Enchanting a stack of e.g. 5 rubies produces 5 enchanted rubies for one gold payment and one enchantment-point budget; DFU enchants exactly one split-off gem.

findings.title: Item maker gold check and label use coins only, excluding letters of credit

The port's gold() (itemMakerWindow.js:189) calls goldAmount(), the coin purse alone (court.js:151-152); enchantDecision's gold test (enchanting.js:188) and the label both ride it. The port's own comment at :282-284 says the deduction seam spends letters of credit - but the gating check never counts them.
findings.consequence: A player whose wealth sits in letters of credit is refused ('You do not have the gold to properly pay the enchanter') where DFU lets the enchant proceed, and the shown gold figure is understated.

findings.title: Cast When Used/Held/Strikes list rows print the wrong spell name
findings.claim: DFU's EnchantmentPanel prints enchantment.SecondaryDisplayName - the actual spell name stored in the settings (EnchantmentListPicker.cs:333-334). The port draws the secondary row as names[row.entry.param] (itemMakerWindow.js:390-393), where names = enchantmentParams(type) is a DENSE list-ordered array (enchantmentCatalogue.js:193-201) but entry.param for the three CastWhen* effects is the sparse classic SPELL ID (catalogue :171, stored at :233). E.g. CastWhenUsed param 12 is Resist Fire, but names[12] is 'Fireball'; param 94 (Recall) indexes past the array and prints blank. The picker itself is correct (labels[i] aligned by index, catalogue :493-495) - only the list rows mis-index.
findings.consequence: After picking 'Cast when used - Resist Fire' the powers list shows 'Fireball' (or a blank) under Cast When Used; nearly every CastWhen* row names the wrong spell.

findings.title: Enchantment lists cannot scroll; overflowing rows are invisible and unremovable
findings.claim: DFU's EnchantmentListPicker shows a slim scrollbar when enchantmentPanels.Count > 7 (ShowScroller, cs:244-247), narrows rows to 71 wide, and scrolls via wheel (MouseScrollUp/Down cs:180-196) and the scroller. The port's draw loop breaks at 'if (row.y + row.h > rect[3]) break' (itemMakerWindow.js:385), computes 'scrolled' and voids it (:383, :395), and neither click() (:338-344) nor input() offers any scroll path for the two lists. With rows carrying secondary names (12px + 5 gap), only 7 rows fit in the 120px rect, so an 8th+ row (reachable: up to 10 enchantments, e.g. eight Cast When Used spells) is off-panel.
findings.consequence: Enchantments past the seventh two-line row can be neither seen nor clicked off; DFU scrolls to them.

findings.claim: DFU's AddRecipeToCauldron: if any recipe ingredient is unmatched it shows GetLocalizedText("reqIngredients") and adds NOTHING (cs:297-301); otherwise it ClearCauldron()s first, adds every ingredient, and sets nameLabel = recipeName (cs:302-308). findings.title: Mixing an empty cauldron shows the failure message instead of doing nothing
findings.claim: DFU's MixButton_OnMouseClick plays the click and only calls MixCauldron() 'if (cauldron.Count > 0)' (cs:396-397). The port's _mix (potionMakerWindow.js:151-169) has no emptiness guard: mixCauldron([]) hashes the empty list, matches no recipe, and the window shows the POTION_FAILED box ('The ingredients you have combined are useless.').
findings.consequence: Clicking MIX (or pressing M/Enter) with an empty pot pops a failure message box that DFU never shows.

findings.title: Enchanted ingredients are not excluded from the potion maker's list
findings.claim: DFU's Refresh collects ingredients with 'if (item.IsIngredient && !item.IsEnchanted)' (cs:148), and the consume walk also passes allowEnchantedItem: false (cs:338, :345). The port's ingredients() (potionMakerWindow.js:125-133) filters with isIngredient(it) alone (potions.js:184 - template flag only), so an enchanted gem (mintable at the port's own item maker, which lists Gems) appears in the ingredient grid and can be added to the cauldron and consumed.
findings.consequence: A player can grind an enchanted ruby into a potion - and the takeOne consumption may instead burn an unenchanted one - where DFU keeps enchanted items out of the pot entirely.

findings.title: Ingredient list never scrolls: this.scroll has no writer
findings.claim: DFU's ingredientsListScroller is a scrolling ItemListScroller (4 rows x 3 cols, cs:226-233) with scroll handling for an arbitrary ingredient count. The port initializes this.scroll = 0 (potionMakerWindow.js:113) and reads it at :216 and :234, but nothing in click() or input() ever modifies it - grep confirms those are the only three references. Only the first 12 ingredient stacks are ever shown or clickable.
findings.consequence: A player holding more than 12 distinct ingredient stacks (routine for an alchemist) can never see or use ingredients 13+, and recipes needing them can only be loaded via the RECIPES button.

findings.title: Adding an ingredient from a stack hides the whole stack (no SplitStack)
findings.claim: DFU's AddToCauldron splits one unit off a stack before moving it: 'if (item.IsAStack()) item = ingredients.SplitStack(item, 1)' (cs:256-257), leaving the remainder visible and addable. The port's _addToCauldron (potionMakerWindow.js:137-141) pushes the stack OBJECT into the cauldron, and ingredients() (:125-133) removes it from the list by identity, so a stack of N elderberries vanishes entirely from the grid while one conceptual unit is in the pot; a second unit of the same stack cannot be added.
findings.consequence: With merged ingredient stacks (the port stacks ingredients per inventory.js:110), the remaining N-1 units are invisible and unusable while one is in the cauldron; DFU shows and offers the remainder.

findings.title: Name label is set on successful mix; DFU sets it only on recipe fill
findings.claim: DFU's MixCauldron never touches nameLabel (cs:311-360); the label is written only by AddRecipeToCauldron ('nameLabel.Text = recipeName', cs:307) and cleared by every add/remove. The port inverts this: _mix sets this.nameLabel = result.recipe.name on success (potionMakerWindow.js:158) while _fillFrom leaves it blank (finding on :184 above). potionmakerwindow.test.js:136 pins the port's mix-time label.
findings.consequence: The bottom-left name label shows the potion name after mixing (it stays blank in DFU) and stays blank after a recipe fill (where DFU shows the recipe name).

findings.title: Potion maker gold label wired to coins only, not GetGoldAmount
findings.claim: DFU's potion maker label reads GameManager.Instance.PlayerEntity.GetGoldAmount() (cs:138), which is goldPieces + letters of credit (PlayerEntity.cs:1313-1316). The host hands the window 'gold: () => goldAmount(playerEntity)' (worldModes.js:1741) - the coin purse only (court.js:151-152) - which potionMakerWindow.js:246 prints.
findings.consequence: The gold figure in the potion maker understates a player's wealth when part of it is letters of credit (display only - no purchase rides it).

findings.title: Sort-by-cost applies the lycanthropy free-cast quirk; DFU sorts by real cost
findings.claim: DFU's SortSpellsPointCost orders by the raw CalculateTotalEffectCosts spell-point cost (DaggerfallEntity.cs:743-748) with no tag check - the lycanthropy 0-display quirk lives only in PopulateSpellsList (DaggerfallSpellBookWindow.cs:264-267). The port's confirmSort cost map uses spellPointCost(sp, castCost) (spellbookWindow.js:511), which returns 0 for the lycanthropy tag (:212-215), so that spell sorts to the front instead of to its true-cost position.
findings.consequence: For a lycanthrope, the second (cost) sort pass places the lycanthropy spell first in the book rather than where its real casting cost puts it in DFU.

findings.title: Spellbook scroll bar is drawn but not interactive
findings.claim: DFU's VerticalScrollBar supports thumb dragging (Update, cs:104-128) and click-above/below-thumb paging by displayUnits (MouseClick, cs:140-148), wired to the list via OnScroll (DaggerfallSpellBookWindow.cs:371, :794-797). The port draws the thumb (spellbookWindow.js:784-789) but click() (:649-705) has no branch for SPELLBOOK_RECTS.scrollBar - a click there falls through to 'return true' with no effect, and there is no drag path.
findings.consequence: With more than 16 spells, clicking or dragging the scroll bar does nothing; only the wheel and arrow buttons scroll, where DFU also pages and drags.

findings.title: Spell maker ignores allowedTargets/allowedElements restrictions from chosen effects
findings.claim: DFU restricts target and element to what the chosen effects allow: SetSpellTarget returns early when '(allowedTargets & targetType) == TargetTypes.None' (cs:499-501), SetSpellElement likewise (cs:527-530), and UpdateAllowedButtons recomputes allowedTargets as the INTERSECTION of each effect's Properties.AllowedTargets and allowedElements as magic-only union (cs:563-601), forcing the selection back to the first allowed value. The port's _inputMain cycles rangeType and element freely through all five values (spellMakerWindow.js:187-190) and no allowedTargets/allowedElements state exists anywhere in src/ (grep confirms).
findings.consequence: The port will price and inscribe combinations DFU forbids - e.g. an 'Area at Range' spell from a caster-only effect - producing spells with wrong target semantics and costs that classic/DFU can never mint.

findings.title: Quest-item transfer guard missing; playerDropped never written, DroppedItemAtPlace can never fire
findings.claim: DFU TransferItem (DaggerfallInventoryWindow.cs:1480-1505) refuses moving a quest item out of the pack when CanDropQuestItems is false (default False in both; port settingsDefaults.js:124) unless questItem.AllowDrop, and on a legal drop sets PlayerDropped=true (:1497-1498), clearing it on pickup (:1499-1500). The port's Remove arm (nativeInventory.js:453-501) and remote pickup (:549-594) guard only Transportation (:464) and summoned (:472). The port's quest Item has playerDropped (quest/item.js:78) and DroppedItemAtPlace reads it (actions.js:1871) - but nothing in src/ ever sets playerDropped=true; its only DFU writer is this missing arm.
findings.consequence: Players can drop/wagon-stash undroppable quest items, and every 'dropped item at place' quest objective is permanently uncompletable - the trigger polls a flag no code path can set.

findings.title: Remote-list quest item click never fires setPlayerClicked
findings.claim: DFU RemoteItemListScroller_OnItemClick's first act (DaggerfallInventoryWindow.cs:2027-2037): if item.IsQuestItem, resolve the quest Item and call SetPlayerClicked() - before any action-mode branch. The port's _pickRemote (nativeInventory.js:549-594) has no such call; setPlayerClicked fires only from world-flat clicks and NPC sweeps (resourceBehaviour.js:148, machine.js:510), never from the inventory window. The ClickedItem trigger consumes item.hasPlayerClicked (systems/quest/actions.js:484).
findings.consequence: A quest item riding a foe (corpse loot) or any loot container: taking it through the loot window adds it to the bag but the 'clicked item' task never triggers - the quest stalls.

findings.title: Sell staging bypasses every TransferItem guard: summoned, quest, loaded-cart, map
findings.claim: DFU's Sell/SellMagic local click routes through TransferItem (DaggerfallTradeWindow.cs:795), inheriting its guards: summoned refused with 'cannotRemoveItem' (DaggerfallInventoryWindow.cs:1464-1469), quest items refused (:1481-1494), maps consumed via RecordLocationFromMap (:1471-1478); the trade window also blocks selling the cart while the wagon holds items (DaggerfallTradeWindow.cs:789-793). The port's _pickLocal (nativeTrade.js:187-199) calls localClickDecision (tradeModes.js:350-371) which answers {kind:'stage'} unconditionally for Sell/SellMagic, and _move (:150-154) is a raw splice/push with no guard.
findings.consequence: Players can sell summoned (soon-to-vanish) items and quest-critical items to shops, and sell the cart out from under a loaded wagon - all refused or special-cased in DFU.

findings.title: TransferItem's map arm missing: maps transfer as items instead of revealing a location
findings.claim: DFU TransferItem's first content arm (DaggerfallInventoryWindow.cs:1471-1478): a MiscItems.Map item transferred in either direction (remove-drop or loot pickup) calls RecordLocationFromMap and removes it - it never lands in the destination. The port implements the reveal only in the Use-mode arm (useItem.js:220-236 via revealMap); _pick's Remove arm (nativeInventory.js:464-501) and _pickRemote (:549-594) transfer a map like any other item.
findings.consequence: Picking a treasure map out of a loot pile (the common classic route) puts the map in the bag instead of revealing a location and consuming it; dropping one stashes it instead of revealing.

findings.title: Lit light source not extinguished when transferred out of the pack
findings.claim: DFU TransferItem (DaggerfallInventoryWindow.cs:1506-1508): 'if (item.IsLightSource && playerEntity.LightSource == item && from == localItems) playerEntity.LightSource = null'. The port tracks entity.lightSource (playerTorch.js:113-135, useItem.js:263-267) but the inventory Remove transfer (nativeInventory.js:482-501) and the trade sell staging (nativeTrade.js:195) never clear it.
findings.consequence: Dropping or selling a lit torch/lantern leaves entity.lightSource pointing at an item no longer carried - the player keeps the light (and its condition burn) from an item lying in a pile or a shop.

findings.title: Buy-mode basket staging skips the CanCarryAmount gate
findings.claim: DFU's Buy remote click transfers shelf->basket through TransferItem with maxAmount=CanCarryAmount(item) (DaggerfallTradeWindow.cs:842): zero capacity shows 'cannotCarryAnymore' and refuses (DaggerfallInventoryWindow.cs:1414-1422), a partial fit splits. The port's _pickRemote (nativeTrade.js:204-209) moves the whole item into the basket with no capacity check.
findings.consequence: A player can stage and buy arbitrarily heavy lots that DFU would refuse or split at basket time, ending up over MaxEncumbrance through the shop screen.

findings.title: Conversation scroll arrows missing; history pinned to newest and unreadable
findings.claim: DFU's talk window has conversation up/down arrows at (303,64,9,16)/(303,176,9,16) (DaggerfallTalkWindow.cs:226-227, wired :798-804) whose handlers move the conversation scrollbar +/-5px (:1442-1452), plus the scrollbar at (305,81). The port's TALK_RECTS (nativeTalk.js:40-57) has no conversation arrows, and draw() recomputes scroll as max(0, contentH - panelH) every frame (:106, :338), permanently pinning the panel to the last row.
findings.consequence: Once the conversation exceeds 126px the player cannot scroll back to re-read earlier answers (directions, names) that DFU keeps reachable.

findings.title: Journal log-entry clicks are inert: no travel-map jump, no move/remove/add-note
findings.claim: DFU's questLogLabel takes clicks and right-clicks (DaggerfallQuestJournalWindow.cs:153-154) into HandleClick (:385-436): on Active Quests a click offers a travel-map jump to the quest's place (FindPlace_OnButtonClick :353-363); on notebook/finished pages click offers move, right-click remove, a click between entries adds a note, and the title-panel click opens EnterNote (:297-300). The port's click() (questJournal.js:182-191) consumes the log and title rects as no-ops and no other member implements these flows.
findings.consequence: Players cannot jump to a quest location from the journal, nor add, move, or remove notebook/finished-quest entries - all standard DFU journal interactions.

findings.title: F6 near a dungeon exit opens wagon in Remove mode; DFU keeps Equip
findings.claim: DFU CheckWagonAccess's proximity branch (DaggerfallInventoryWindow.cs:1089-1096) only sets allowDungeonWagonAccess and ShowWagon(true) - the action mode stays the Equip default from OnPush (:649-653). SelectActionMode(Remove) happens only in the first branch (:1084-1088), reached via the exit-door prompt's AllowDungeonWagonAccess (PlayerActivate.cs:1141). The port's constructor (nativeInventory.js:218-219) merges both flows: a near-exit open sets usingWagon AND mode='remove'.
findings.consequence: Opening inventory near a dungeon exit with a cart, a local-list click transfers the item into the wagon instead of equipping it - the opposite default of DFU's plain F6 flow.

findings.title: chooseOne: DFU blocks all local Remove transfers; port allows staging into the wagon
findings.claim: DFU's local Remove arm runs only 'if (remoteItems != null && !chooseOne)' (DaggerfallInventoryWindow.cs:1994) - while a choose-one reward list is up nothing leaves the pack regardless of wagon state. The port's guard (nativeInventory.js:474) is 'if (this.chooseOne && !this.usingWagon) return', and _wagon (:381-393) has no chooseOne gate, so a cart owner can toggle the wagon and transfer pack items into it mid-choose-one.
findings.consequence: During a guild reward choose-one window, a cart owner can move pack items into the wagon where DFU makes the local list inert.

findings.title: Journal highlight tokens draw orange; DFU overrides HighlightColor to white here
findings.claim: The port's JOURNAL_COLORS.highlight is (219,130,40), citing DaggerfallHighlightTextColor as the MultiFormatTextLabel default (questJournal.js:69-80). But DaggerfallQuestJournalWindow.cs:152 explicitly sets 'questLogLabel.HighlightColor = Color.white', so TextHighlight tokens (date/city and finished-quest headers) render white in this window (MultiFormatTextLabel.cs:362-364 uses HighlightColor).
findings.consequence: Every notebook date header and finished-quest header shows orange where DFU shows white.

findings.title: Character sheet stat labels lack drained/increased colors
findings.claim: DFU UpdatePlayerValues (DaggerfallCharacterSheetWindow.cs:414-419) colors each stat label DaggerfallUnityStatDrainedTextColor (190,85,24) when live < permanent and DaggerfallUnityStatIncreasedTextColor (178,207,255) when live > permanent (DaggerfallUI.cs:65-66). The port draws all eight stats via label() with the shadowText default color (charsheet.js:289-290; nativePanel.js:24, :87).
findings.consequence: A player with drained (disease/spell) or fortified stats sees them in the normal yellow - the at-a-glance drain warning DFU gives is absent.

findings.title: Conversation questions left-aligned; DFU right-aligns question rows
findings.claim: DFU SetQuestionAnswerPairInConversationListbox sets the question label's HorizontalAlignment to Right (DaggerfallTalkWindow.cs:1259) while answers are Left (:1270). The port draws every conversation line at the panel's left edge R.conversation[0] (nativeTalk.js:344-345) regardless of kind.
findings.consequence: The classic visual distinction (player questions hugging the right margin, NPC answers the left) is lost in the conversation log.

findings.title: Nature scatter rect exclusion gated on pre-expansion mins; DFU re-checks the expanded rect per tile
findings.claim: DFU LayoutNature expands the location rect by natureClearance=4 only when the un-expanded rect has x>0 && y>0 (TerrainNature.cs:60-66), then in the tile loop re-evaluates `rect.x > 0 && rect.y > 0 && rect.Contains(tilePos)` on the EXPANDED rect (TerrainNature.cs:124) - so when expansion pushes xMin or yMin to <= 0, DFU disables the containment test entirely and scatters nature inside the location footprint. The port (terrainNature.js:72-79) builds the rect when the PRE-expansion mins are > 0 and then applies containment unconditionally at line 112, never re-checking the expanded mins.
findings.consequence: For a location whose pre-clearance rect min on either axis lies in (0, 4] (only possible for 8-block-wide/tall locations, since the tile origin is 0 only then), DFU places nature billboards over the town footprint while the port suppresses them - a visible foliage difference at large walled cities with narrow edge blend space.

findings.title: envAttack skips Receive(Attack) on doors; DFU fires the door's action record before bashing

So an Attack/MultiTrigger-flagged door record (Castle Wayrest doors are MultiTrigger, DaggerfallActionDoor.cs:263 comment) never fires on a weapon hit; the bash path's _execOwnAction passes only the 'Door' trigger, which those flags reject. test/weaponrig.test.js:83 pins the port's behavior, restating the port.

findings.title: Dungeon castle/special-area ambient (0.58) unported - castle blocks render at 0.12

findings.title: Door close sound fires at swing start; DFU plays it when the close completes
findings.claim: DFU Close() (:311-332) starts the reverse tween and plays NO sound; CloseSound plays in OnCompleteClose (:339-346), after the 1.5 s swing, just before the collider re-solidifies. The port's _closeDoor (actionSystem.js:656-657) emits onDoorState(o, false) at close START and both hosts play the clip immediately (dungeonContext.js:199-202, interiorContext.js:51-54). Open-side timing matches DFU (sound at open start, :296-302 vs actionSystem.js:645).
findings.consequence: Every door close is audible ~1.5 s early - the shut sound plays while the door is still swinging instead of when it lands closed as in DFU.

findings.title: Port persists activationCount across save/load; DFU resets it to 0
findings.claim: SerializableActionObject (:55-88) persists only position/rotation/currentState/tween percentage; SerializableActionDoor (:67-101) adds lock and FailedSkillLevel. Neither serializes DaggerfallAction.activationCount, and the scene rebuilds on load, so every counter restarts at 0 in DFU. The port saves it for every object (actionSystem.js:830-832) and restores it (:858-859). Save-relevant state semantics are in the byte-exact doctrine list.
findings.consequence: After loading, DFU re-shows a DoorText door's text and holds it shut on first click, and restarts Hurt21's every-20th phase; the port does neither, so trap cadence and first-click door behavior diverge after any save/load.

findings.title: LightningPlayer slots are always 2 frames; DFU's skipped flash is a 1-frame slot
findings.claim: DFU PlayLightningEffects (:367-382): per flash, `if (Random.value < 0.6) { on; yield; }` then unconditionally off + yield - a skipped flash consumes ONE frame, a lit one two. The port (weather.js:169-179) always spends two frames per slot, and its comment claims parity with 'the coroutine's WaitForEndOfFrame pairs'. Also DFU re-arms the next 4-35 s wait at strike time (:146-152), while the port re-arms after the sequence ends (:176-179).
findings.consequence: Storm flash sequences run up to ~2x the frames of DFU (a 20-30 flash roll is ~0.3-0.5 s longer at 60 fps) and successive strikes drift slightly later; visual timing only.

findings.title: failedSkillLevel omitted from save snapshot (in-code FLAGGED gap, confirmed)
